title: NRIC Numbers in ACRA's Bizfile Service
what_it_is: NRIC Numbers in ACRA's Bizfile Service

sections.label: NRIC numbers in Bizfile People Search
sections.summary: NRIC numbers were fully shown in ACRA's free People Search from 9 to 13 December 2024; after suspension, results no longer show NRIC numbers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Many Singaporeans regard NRIC numbers as sensitive information and are understandably concerned to learn that NRIC numbers were available in full in the free People Search function of ACRA's new Bizfile portal from 9 to 13 December 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In the wake of the public concern about the disclosure, ACRA suspended the service and since the resumption of service on 28 December 2024, the search results under the revised People Search function no longer show any NRIC numbers, masked or unmasked.

sections.label: ACRA allowed to disclose NRIC numbers
sections.summary: ACRA is allowed by law to give public access to information including NRIC numbers to maintain corporate transparency and guard against illicit activities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To maintain corporate transparency, facilitate business transactions and guard against illicit activities, ACRA is allowed by law to give public access to such information, including NRIC numbers.

sections.label: Disclosure not prohibited per se
sections.summary: Public disclosure of NRIC numbers is not prohibited per se; the real issue is the degree and ease of access.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In summary, therefore, it is important to understand that the public disclosure of NRIC numbers is not prohibited per se.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The real issue is the degree and the ease of access to NRIC numbers.

sections.label: Revised People Search returns names only
sections.summary: ACRA revised the People Search function so it only returns names and displays no NRIC numbers, masked or unmasked.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: ACRA has since revised the People Search function such that it only returns names and no longer displays any NRIC numbers, whether masked or unmasked.

sections.label: MDDI circular minute on NRIC use
sections.summary: In July 2024 MDDI directed all Government agencies to stop using NRIC numbers as authenticators and cease planned use of masked NRIC numbers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Consequently, in July 2024, MDDI issued a circular minute directing all Government agencies to: one, stop using NRIC numbers as authenticators or passwords; and two, cease any planned use of masked NRIC numbers in, for example, new business processes and digital services.

sections.label: ACRA mistakenly unmasked NRIC numbers
sections.summary: Due to a lapse in coordination, ACRA mistakenly understood MDDI's directive as requiring full NRIC numbers, and disclosed them on 9 December 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: ACRA then sought MDDI's clarification on whether it was required to unmask NRIC numbers in the People Search function on the new Bizfile portal.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, due to a lapse in coordination between MDDI and ACRA, ACRA continued to understand, mistakenly, that the directive to cease the use of masked NRIC numbers in new digital services required ACRA to unmask and disclose in full the NRIC numbers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Hence, ACRA disclosed full NRIC numbers in the People Search function when the new Bizfile portal was launched on 9 December 2024, as they thought MDDI required them to.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Minister Josephine Teo has since explained, both at the press conference on 19 December 2024 and in her Ministerial Statement earlier, that when MDDI told agencies to cease the use of masked NRIC numbers, that did not automatically mean using full NRIC numbers in every case.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Instead, MDDI's policy intent was for agencies to: one, not use NRIC numbers at all unless necessary; two, use other identifiers in lieu of NRIC numbers, where this was adequate; and three, in certain cases, such as in medical settings, where the use of NRIC numbers is required by law or necessary for accurate identification, use full NRIC numbers.

sections.label: Function disabled 13 December 2024
sections.summary: The function was disabled on the night of 13 December 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The function was disabled on the night of 13 December 2024.

sections.label: People Search query volume
sections.summary: More than 500,000 queries were made on People Search from 9 to 13 December 2024, higher than the usual 2,000 to 3,000 daily queries.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Based on the investigations so far, more than 500,000 queries were made on People Search during that five-day period from 9 to 13 December 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This was much higher than the usual daily traffic of 2,000 to 3,000 queries.

sections.label: Security feature not working
sections.summary: ACRA and GovTech's security review found the People Search feature designed to distinguish humans from bots was not working as intended.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: ACRA and GovTech have since conducted a security review and identified that the security feature in the People Search function designed to distinguish between human users and computer bots was not working as intended.

sections.label: Review panel set up
sections.summary: A review panel has been set up to study the root cause of the incident, and work is already underway.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, a review panel has been set up to study the root cause of the incident, and work is already underway.

sections.label: Panel review matters
sections.summary: The panel will review the Government's policy on responsible use of NRIC numbers and the disclosure of full NRIC numbers on People Search.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The panel will review two matters: first, the Government’s policy on the responsible use of NRIC numbers; and second, the disclosure of full NRIC numbers on the People Search function of ACRA’s new Bizfile portal.

sections.label: Review completion in February
sections.summary: The panel expects to complete its review in February.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The panel expects to complete its review in February.

sections.label: PDPA, PSGA and Government IMs
sections.summary: The PDPA applies to the private sector, while public agencies like ACRA are governed by the PSGA and Government IMs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The PDPA applies to the private sector, whereas public agencies like ACRA are governed by the PSGA and the Government IMs.

sections.label: ACRA NRIC unmasking cause
sections.summary: The unmasking of NRIC numbers in People Search arose from ACRA's misunderstanding of MDDI's policy intent and gaps in communication and coordination between agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The unmasking of NRIC numbers in the People Search function arose from ACRA's misunderstanding of MDDI's policy intent, and gaps in communication and coordination between agencies.

sections.label: NRIC policy stance change question
sections.summary: A key issue is whether the policy stance changed, given past comfort with sharing NRIC numbers, later sensitisation under PDPA, and a PDPA guideline on collection and retention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: First of all, one of the key issues that we have seen here is the question of, "Has the policy stance changed?" Prior to the introduction of PDPA, Singaporeans were quite comfortable with sharing their NRIC numbers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Then, later, we were cultivated to be sensitised to NRIC numbers, especially in the period of introducing PDPA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: So, now, with the latest incident, naturally, Singaporeans will wonder, "Is there a change and why is there a change?" And compounding this was that there was a guideline on the collection and retention of NRIC numbers, as part of the guidelines under PDPA.

sections.label: Questions on NRIC safeguards and review
sections.summary: The passage asks about actions to safeguard information, the timeline for engaging organisations using NRIC numbers for authentication, why past practices were not pursued, and fairness to civil servants in the review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: What would be helpful is to share what kind of actions will be put in place to safeguard such information and prevent such misuses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And from now till then, as the Ministry goes out to engage organisations that are currently using NRIC numbers for authentication, not just for passwords or default passwords but also as default identification, or ID, what is the period of time that the Ministry is looking at to quickly get these organisations to rectify it, so that it would help to alleviate the concerns and anxiety that Singaporeans may have during this period?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Thirdly, if NRIC numbers are not meant to be used as an authenticator, then in the past few years, why did the Government not actively go after organisations that have been implementing such practices?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Would it be seen as implicitly endorsing this understanding?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And lastly, I am glad that there will be a review panel to establish the facts of the matter, but at the same time, I also would like to urge the Government to be fair to the civil servants, especially ACRA in this instance, especially if they had no ill intent.

sections.label: Withdrawal of NRIC Guidelines
sections.summary: The PDPC's Guidelines on NRIC were withdrawn for a very short period to apply a new label drawing attention to subsequent statements.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Ms Tin had a specific question on the Guidelines on NRIC that are issued by PDPC and why were they withdrawn?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It was withdrawn for a very short period of time to apply a new label to it, to draw people's attention to the statements that were made subsequently.

sections.label: NRIC numbers not authenticators
sections.summary: Few scams pinpoint an NRIC number unlocking valuables, so organisations should not use NRIC numbers as authenticators or default passwords and individuals should not use them as passwords.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Very few of the scams, in fact, it is not quite so easy to pinpoint even one specific instance, where the scammer was able to get hold of the NRIC number and then key that in to unlock valuables.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, it goes back to the best protection that we can have for each other, and that is: for organisations, not to use NRIC numbers as authenticators or default passwords; and for individuals, not to use these NRIC numbers as passwords.

sections.label: Stopping incorrect NRIC uses
sections.summary: The change concerns only stopping incorrect uses of NRIC numbers as authenticators and passwords.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The change is only in respect of stopping the incorrect uses of NRIC numbers as authenticators and as passwords.

sections.label: Panel findings and referrals
sections.summary: The incident appears to be miscommunication, but if the panel finds actionable wrongdoing or serious lapses, it will refer the matter to authorities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, based on the preliminary findings, the incident seems to be a genuine case of miscommunication, but at the same time we do not want to prejudge the issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, as I also mentioned, if the panel uncovers facts that suggest actionable wrongdoing or serious lapses, then it will refer the matter to relevant bodies or authorities for further action.

sections.label: Bill groundwork for Bizfile
sections.summary: Minister Indranee confirmed the Bill laid the groundwork for the enhanced Bizfile system targeted for launch at the end of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister Indranee, in moving the Bill, confirmed that the Bill laid the groundwork for the enhanced Bizfile system that was targeted for launch at the end of 2024.

sections.label: ACRA consultation on masking numbers
sections.summary: ACRA proposed partially masking identification numbers in its public registers and introducing a public contact address, drawing feedback on corporate transparency and know-your-client requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this consultation, ACRA had proposed, "to partially mask the identification numbers of all individuals in ACRA's registers which are made available to the public and introduce a contact address that will be shown to the public." There was some feedback to this proposal, principally related to corporate transparency and know-your-client requirements.

sections.label: Public consultation summary issued
sections.summary: The summary of the public consultation was issued in April 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, the summary of the public consultation was issued in April 2024.

sections.label: ACRA proceeds with contact address
sections.summary: ACRA proceeded with the contact address as default public address, and noted concerns on requiring access to full identification numbers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: ACRA's response was to proceed with the proposal to introduce a contact address as the default address of individuals that will be shown to the public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On the proposal to mask identification numbers, the concerns on requiring access to full identification numbers have been duly noted.

sections.label: Ministry circular on masking NRIC
sections.summary: The passage asks when the Ministry circular seeking to change NRIC masking practice was dated and communicated to Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: To ask the Minister of Digital Development and Information, when was the Ministry circular that sought to change the practice of masking NRIC numbers dated and communicated to Government agencies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I think Minister answered by saying July 2024.

sections.label: Algorithms deriving full NRIC numbers
sections.summary: The passage states that algorithms available online can derive full NRIC numbers, particularly if the birth year is known.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The same could apply to partial NRIC numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I explained earlier in my Ministerial Statement that what has happened is that nowadays, there are quite easily available online, algorithms that can allow you to guess, or work out, or derive, the full NRIC number, particularly if you know the birth year of a person.

sections.label: Masked NRIC false sense of security
sections.summary: The passage states that masked NRIC numbers give a false sense of security because algorithms can derive full NRIC numbers, risking scams and identity theft.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In which case, a person who is determined to work out the full NRIC number of these individuals from the masked NRIC number or the partial NRIC number, could quite easily use these algorithms to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, the ease of availability of such algorithms will mean that the continued use of masked NRIC number gives this false sense of security that will not go away.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And if this false sense of security were to persist and people think that their full NRIC number is still a secret, and they continue to use it as a password or if organisations set it as a default password or use it as an authenticator, that is where the risk of scams is, that is where the risk of harms associated with identity theft will become more commonplace.

sections.label: Notifications and NRIC authenticator timeline
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government would notify all households about the incident and whether a timeline was given to stop using NRIC as an authenticator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The first is that I understand that there were about 500,000 queries, but given that we do not know actually whose NRIC number was being accessed, would the Government consider issuing individual notifications to all the different households in the four major languages, just to inform them of this incident and the necessary precautions that need to be taken just to ensure that people are prepared?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I think there was a Straits Times article that talked about how it can be used to access bank information and healthcare records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And so, has the Government given a timeline for both the Public Healthcare Institutions or private financial institutions to stop the use of the NRIC as an authenticator?

sections.label: Bizfile NRIC numbers and public education
sections.summary: The passage clarifies that Bizfile NRIC numbers are not all Singaporeans' and advises not using NRIC as a password or authenticator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The first thing to clarify is that the NRIC numbers in Bizfile are not the NRIC numbers of all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The other thing to bear in mind is that those who have incorporated a business or have taken on board directorships and so on, and have their information with ACRA, would know that the information can be made publicly available.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I think the better approach is really this – for everybody who has provided information in lodgements or filings with ACRA to take heed of what we have indicated, which is: one, do not use your NRIC as a password or authenticator; two, be careful if somebody comes citing your NRIC number asking you to do something, and this will be part and parcel of the public education that we will put out.

sections.label: Specific cases for full NRIC use
sections.summary: The passage asks for help in understanding the specific cases where full NRIC numbers will be used as an additional identifier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In view of Minister Teo's clarification that the Government is not moving to a widespread disclosure of full NRIC numbers in its transactions with citizens going forward, but only to use full NRIC numbers as an additional identifier in specific cases where this is actually necessary, it will be very helpful to help the public understand just what these specific cases might be.

sections.label: Public sector ceased NRIC authenticators
sections.summary: Following a circular, all public sector agencies have ceased using NRIC numbers as authenticators.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: What I can share with her is that following the circular that was sent out, to the best of our knowledge, all Government, all public sector agencies have ceased the use of NRIC number as authenticators.

sections.label: NRIC as Singpass default identifier
sections.summary: Singpass designers needed a unique identifier, so the NRIC number is used as the default identifier.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In making Singpass available, designers have to find a way to have a unique identifier and so the NRIC number is used as the default identifier.

sections.label: Singpass user ID change allowed
sections.summary: Singpass allows anyone to change their user ID to something other than their NRIC number.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Although it is the default identifier, Singpass allows anyone to change out their user ID to something that is not their NRIC number.

sections.label: Findings will be made public
sections.summary: The findings will be made public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What I said just now and what will be accurate for me to say is that the findings will be made public.

sections.label: ACRA disclosed NRIC numbers fully
sections.summary: Gaps in coordination led ACRA to misunderstand requirements and disclose NRIC numbers in full at its Bizfile portal launch.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In this process of implementation, there were gaps in coordination and these resulted in ACRA misunderstanding what was required of them and disclosing the NRIC numbers in full when they launched their new Bizfile portal.

sections.label: Digital NRIC card as authenticator
sections.summary: Producing the digital NRIC card is the same as the physical card, so it would be acceptable as an authenticator, and there was a response when ACRA sought clarification.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In fact, we have said quite clearly that the production of this digital NRIC card is the same as producing the physical NRIC card.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, it would be acceptable as an authenticator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, let me deal with the issue of whether there was a response when ACRA sought clarification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: There was a response, and I understand that the communications continued for a while.

sections.label: ACRA coordination and policy intent
sections.summary: ACRA had concerns, but there was no clear understanding of policy intent and sometimes a lapse of coordination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is not like they did not talk, because ACRA did have some concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But what is very clear is that there was not a clear understanding of the policy intent and in some cases, it really was a lapse of coordination.

sections.label: ACRA personal information public
sections.summary: Anyone who provided personal information in a document or lodgement with ACRA would know that information is available publicly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Anybody who has provided personal information in a document or lodgement with ACRA would know that actually that information is available publicly.

sections.label: ACRA information permitted public
sections.summary: If the claim is that the NRIC number was made public, the suggestion is that is wrong, but ACRA information is permitted to be made public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, if the claim is that the NRIC number was made public, then the suggestion is that it is wrong to make it public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But information held by ACRA is actually permitted to be made public.

sections.label: Unknown access and public information
sections.summary: At the moment you do not know whose information has been accessed, but such information can be publicly accessible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The short answer to the question is, at the moment, you do not even know whose information has been accessed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But second, insofar as the suggestion is that the information cannot be made public, the answer is that such information can be publicly accessible.

sections.label: House visits for seniors
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to consider using Silver Generation Office or SG Digital Office for house visits to explain to seniors and hard-to-reach segments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry also consider using Silver Generation Office or the SG Digital Office to do house visits and sort of explain this to seniors?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: He is right to say that there will be certain hard-to-reach segments: seniors, perhaps persons with less privileged backgrounds.

sections.label: Government knowledge of NRIC authentication
sections.summary: Minister Josephine Teo is asked how long the Government knew organisations used NRIC numbers as an authentication factor and why it did not prohibit this before December 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, for Minister Josephine Teo, how long has the Government known that organisations, including those in the public sector, have been using NRIC numbers as an authentication factor and why did it not prohibit its use long before December 2024?

sections.label: Legal prohibition of NRIC authenticators
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will legally prohibit its agencies and organisations from using NRIC numbers as authenticators by a deadline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the Government legally prohibit Government agencies and organisations from using NRIC numbers as authenticators and do so by a certain deadline?

sections.label: Randomly generating NRIC numbers
sections.summary: The passage asks what prevents the NRIC number from being randomly generated going forward instead of relying on an algorithm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My question is: what prevents the NRIC number from being randomly generated, moving forward, instead of relying on an algorithm?

sections.label: Problem relatively contained
sections.summary: The passage states that, as said in a Ministerial Statement, the problem is relatively contained.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As I said in my Ministerial Statement, the problem is relatively contained.

sections.label: Advice against NRIC authentication
sections.summary: The passage advises that NRIC numbers are not a good authenticator and should not be used, and that private sector practices will be decided upon consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If they still choose, for whatever services that they make available digitally to their clients or to their stakeholders, to require authentication, then, our advice to them is that the NRIC number is not a very good authenticator, they should not use it at all.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As to the question of whether we will legally prohibit the use of NRIC numbers as authenticators, as I said, the practices for the private sector will have to be decided upon consultation.

sections.label: Bizfile portal filing extension
sections.summary: The passage states ACRA gave an extension of time to users who need to file documents and indicated no late penalties will be imposed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Okay, on that, I understand that there have been some initial issues with the new Bizfile portal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: However, what ACRA has done is that they have given an extension of time to users who need to file the documents and they have also indicated that no late penalties will be imposed on people who have difficulties with filing.

sections.label: Identification not authentication
sections.summary: The passage states the NRIC number has to be used for identification, and it is authentication that it should not be used for.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, it has to be used for identification.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is authentication that it should not be used for.

sections.label: Stopping NRIC numbers as authenticators
sections.summary: The only change being made is to stop incorrect uses of NRIC numbers as authenticators and passwords.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The only change that we are making is to stop the incorrect uses of NRIC numbers as authenticators and as passwords.

sections.label: No full NRIC disclosure
sections.summary: The change does not allow full NRIC numbers to become widely disclosed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To reiterate, we are not making a change to allow full NRIC numbers to become widely disclosed.

sections.label: Identifying individuals in business registers
sections.summary: A business or corporate register requires knowing and identifying the specific individual or entity you are dealing with.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, you need to know which Mr Wong it is, because if your renovations were not done properly and you need to claim a refund or sue him, for example, you need to know whom you are dealing with.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, it is the essence of a business register or corporate register that you must know and be able to identify the specific individual or entity that you are dealing with.

sections.label: Political officeholders and circular minute
sections.summary: No political officeholders were involved in the circular minute or gave directions, and the Member should await the after-action review findings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As far as I am aware, no political officeholders were involved in the circular minute or gave directions on it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But I also said just now that the Member should wait for the findings of the after-action review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This is as much as I know and I am not purporting to be the complete encyclopedia of everything that has happened because there is currently an ongoing review.
